mainEntity.name: Is it better to do a small patch or a continuous flood cut?

acceptedAnswer.text: A partial patch is suitable for isolated leaks that affect only a small area, whereas a flood cut is necessary when standing water touches the floor or moisture wicks upward across a room. The practical tradeoff comes down to cost versus seamless appearance. Patching a small hole requires less demolition, but blending multiple small patches can result in visible seams. A uniform flood cut—removing a continuous horizontal strip 2 or 4 feet up—provides clean access to studs, simplifies insulation installation, and often yields a smoother, faster finish.
acceptedAnswer.description: Small patches work for isolated leaks. A continuous flood cut (cutting 2 to 4 feet up) is cleaner, faster, and better for rising water or widespread moisture issues.
